dedupe_keys.name: epa environmental justice primer for ports the good neighbor guide to building partnerships and social equity with communities 2020

description: The Environmental Justice Primer for Ports (EPA-420-B-20-007, March 2020) was produced by the US Environmental Protection Agency's Office of Transportation and Air Quality to help port decision-makers understand and address the needs of near-port communities. Contents: Section A explains environmental justice principles and how they apply to port operations; Section B is a six-step roadmap for community engagement, partnership building and better quality-of-life outcomes, with case studies of ports at different stages, fillable worksheets and an appendix with a timeline of the environmental justice movement; it complements the Ports Primer for Communities and the Community Action Roadmap, and a training module and toolkit came from pilot projects. It notes that port operations and freight movement cause cumulative air, water, land and land-use impacts on nearby communities. Coverage: US ports and goods movement. Format and access: a 48-page PDF and web pages; the live EPA pages returned 'not found' in September 2026, so the record points to EPA's January 2021 archive and a draft on NEPIS. Licence and cost: free US government work. Caveats: guidance, not a demographic dataset. It frames social vulnerability and engagement for hazard exposure and climate adaptation studies of ports. It relates to the US ports EJSCREEN screening study in the catalogue.
